content.title: About
content.content: Meatless bacon strips are a plant‑based alternative to traditional smoked bacon, made from soy protein, wheat gluten and natural flavorings that mimic the characteristic taste and aroma of cured pork. The product becomes crisp when fried and is suitable for vegetarians and vegans.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Meatless bacon is often produced by vegan brands to give bacon lovers a cruelty‑free option.
Its texture is achieved through extrusion of soy protein followed by smoking.
It contains less saturated fat than conventional pork bacon.
Flavor is enhanced with natural smoke flavor, sea salt and other aromatics.
Meatless bacon can be used in the same dishes as regular bacon: salads, sandwiches, pastas and breakfast plates.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: The plant‑based version contains mostly poly‑ and monounsaturated fats, which are healthier for the cardiovascular system.

items.title: Source of plant protein
items.content: Soy protein provides a complete amino‑acid profile, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Cholesterol‑free
items.content: Unlike pork bacon, meatless bacon contains no cholesterol, which can benefit blood lipid levels.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: The product is often fortified with vitamin B12 and niacin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Reduced sodium options
items.content: Some brands offer low‑salt versions, helpful for people managing blood pressure.

items.title: Soy or gluten allergy
items.content: Contains soy protein and wheat gluten, which may trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Certain varieties can be high in salt; choose reduced‑sodium options if you need to limit sodium intake.

items.title: Processed ingredients
items.content: As with many meat substitutes, the product undergoes processing, which may not suit those preferring whole foods.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Fry the meatless bacon strips in a dry skillet or bake until crispy. Add them to salads, sandwiches, pasta, omelets, or use as a topping for pizza and fries.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the unopened package in a cool, dry place away from direct light. After opening, store in the refrigerator in an airtight container and consume within 7‑10 days.

content.title: About
content.content: Ready‑to‑heat mashed potato (NFS) is a fully prepared product made from selected potatoes that are steamed and pureed without artificial preservatives. It has a smooth, creamy flavor and soft texture, suitable as a side dish or a stand‑alone meal.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Potato is the fourth most produced agricultural crop worldwide after rice, wheat and corn.
Ready‑made mashed potatoes are widely used in cafeterias and restaurants to speed up service.
The NFS (Not From Scratch) concept means the product is ready to eat without any further preparation.
When stored properly, the mash retains a high amount of vitamin C and potassium.
Small amounts of vegetable oils are often added to improve flavor and mouthfeel.

items.title: Rich source of potassium
items.content: Potatoes are high in potassium, which supports normal heart function and muscle activity.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Mashed potato provides vitamin B6 and B3, important for metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: When not overloaded with added butter or oil, the mash contains little saturated fat.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: The soft texture and pre‑cooking make it gentle on the digestive system, ideal for those with chewing difficulties.

items.title: Quick energy source
items.content: Carbohydrates in the mash supply fast‑acting energy, useful for post‑exercise recovery.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some ready‑to‑heat versions contain added salt; people with hypertension should monitor portion size.

items.title: Allergy to additives
items.content: The product may contain dairy or vegetable oils that can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Shelf life
items.content: After opening, keep the mash refrigerated and consume within a few days to prevent bacterial growth.

items.title: Vitamin C loss
items.content: Vitamin C is heat‑sensitive, so processing and storage can reduce its levels.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the mash in the microwave or on the stovetop, stirring until smooth. Add butter, cheese, herbs or spices to taste. It works well as a side for meat or fish dishes or as a light standalone meal.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened package in a cool, dry place. Once opened, keep it in an airtight container in the refrigerator and use within 3‑4 days. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or discoloration.

topping-from-meat-and-vegetable-pizza.title: Topping from meat and vegetable pizza

content.title: About
content.content: The topping from meat and vegetable pizza is a blend of selected cooked meat pieces (such as ham, chicken, or beef) and fresh vegetables (tomatoes, bell pepper, onion, mushrooms). It is made from ingredients already used on pizza and is intended to be added to the finished dish to boost flavor and increase nutritional value.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The topping is often served as a separate side in fast‑food restaurants, allowing customers to add it to any pizza.
The meat‑vegetable combination provides a balance of protein, vitamins, and minerals.
Traditionally only ingredients that have already been heat‑treated are used, making the product safe for reheating.
In some countries the topping is sold frozen, simplifying storage and transport.
Flavor variety is achieved by using different types of meat and seasonal vegetables.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Meat pieces provide high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat contains vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals from vegetables
items.content: Vegetables add vitamin C, vitamin A, potassium, and fiber, which support immunity and digestion.

items.title: Low in simple sugars
items.content: The topping contains no added sugar, making it suitable for moderate‑carb diets.

items.title: Promotes satiety
items.content: The combination of protein and fiber helps keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: Allergy to meat or vegetables
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to specific meats or vegetables included in the mix.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Prepared topping often contains added salt; people monitoring sodium intake should watch portion size.

items.title: Bacterial contamination risk
items.content: If not stored properly, harmful bacteria can grow, especially at temperatures above 4 °C.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Commercial versions may contain preservatives that can affect those with sensitivities.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Add the topping to a ready pizza and heat in the oven or microwave, or use it as a filling for sandwiches, salads, or pasta. When serving, heat to an internal temperature of at least 75 °C.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the topping in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0–4 °C for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze in a freezer‑safe bag at –18 °C, where it retains quality for up to 2 months. Reheat thoroughly before consumption.
